rule.description: Flag local struct/enum/union types whose aggregated inherent impl blocks declare an oversized interface (at least 10 associated functions) that references at least 7 distinct crate-local nominal types defined outside the type's own module, spanning at least 5 distinct foreign modules. One diagnostic is emitted per flagged type, prefixed with the marker `smellbench_god_class:`.

checks.description: Run the Dylint lint `gotham_god_class` over the gotham package and search the output for the `smellbench_god_class:` marker, expecting exactly the gotham/src/router/mod.rs inherent impl of `Router` to be flagged on the injected state, nothing on the clean state, and nothing after the canonical repair.
checks.detected_relation: The `Router` type's inherent impl aggregates 16 associated functions whose bodies reference 9 distinct crate-local nominal types defined in 8 modules other than `router` (state, state::client_addr, state::request_id, helpers::http, helpers::http::request::path, router::non_match, router::response::finalizer, router::tree).
checks.why_this_is_the_smell: The routing type has become the framework's request-lifecycle god class: request correlation metadata access, client address access, path and query parsing, and every category of response synthesis now live as inherent associated functions of the router, interleaved with its original dispatch and finalization logic, while the modules that own those responsibilities were reduced to one-line delegations. No other type in the clean crate reaches these thresholds, and none of the 13 absorbed functions is used by the router's callers directly — they exist only to centralize unrelated responsibilities behind one interface.

matches.evidence: cargo dylint --lib gotham_god_class -p gotham on the injected tree emits one warning at gotham/src/router/mod.rs:142 (the `impl Router` block): `smellbench_god_class: `router::Router` aggregates a god-class interface: 16 associated functions reach across 9 crate-local types defined in 8 other modules (methods=[client_addr,dispatch,empty_response,ensure_request_id,finalize_response,new,non_match_response,not_found_response,path_segments,permanent_redirect,redirect_response,request_id,response,split_query_string,subsegments,temporary_redirect] ...)`. The same command on the pinned clean tree emits no diagnostic, and emits none again after the canonical repair is applied.
